name: King of Jericho
overview: The King of Jericho was a male ruler who held authority during the time of Israel's entry into the Promised Land. While his tribal affiliation is not recorded, he is noted specifically in the context of the conquest period. There are no additional personal details or notes provided about him in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Jericho' simply denotes his position as the monarch over the city of Jericho. This title is descriptive and does not carry a special Hebrew or Greek meaning beyond identifying his role as king, as referenced in Joshua 2:3.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for the King of Jericho beyond his role as the city's ruler during Israel's arrival. No further relational details are given.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Jericho is significant as the reigning authority opposing Israel at the moment they entered the Promised Land. His presence marks the beginning of Israel's military campaign to claim the land God promised to His people. Although little else is known about him, his role sets the stage for the pivotal events that follow in the conquest narrative.
